papers_read.title_as_printed: Deep learning-based classification of healthy aging controls, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease using fusion of MRI-PET imaging (Rallabandi & Seetharaman, 2023, doi 10.1016/j.bspc.2022.104312, file S1746809422007662)

Segmental disturbance of white matter microstructure in predicting mild cognitive impairment in idiopathic Parkinson's disease: An individualized study based on automated fiber quantification tractography (Yu et al., Parkinsonism and Related Disorders 115 (2023) 105802)

what_each_reports.P-117: The record's P-117 (summaries.md S1746809423005462: resting-state EEG, VMD + NSGA-II, best ~99.8% accuracy, sample not reported) could not be checked; the pack PDF is a different paper (OASIS MRI-PET fusion, 95.5% HC vs MCI accuracy, AUC 0.988).
what_each_reports.P-91: DTI automated fiber quantification in idiopathic Parkinson's disease; SVM on segmental FA/MD plus clinical features separating IPD-MCI (n=30) from IPD with normal cognition (n=40), 70/30 split. Validation AUC 0.80, balanced accuracy 0.79 (training AUC 0.82).

quantity_a: Record's P-117: EEG classifier accuracy, MCI vs cognitively healthy older adults, own cohort, internal validation (summary block only).
quantity_b: P-91: SVM ROC-AUC, Parkinson's-disease MCI vs Parkinson's disease with normal cognition, 70 IPD patients, internal 30% hold-out.
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable: accuracy vs AUC are different metric types, and the comparison (PD-MCI vs PD-NCI) and population (Parkinson's disease) differ from MCI vs healthy controls.

gates.task: nominal match (both coded T1) but the comparison differs: PD-MCI vs PD-NCI within Parkinson's disease, not MCI vs healthy controls
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: China Medical University IPD cohort vs P-117's EEG cohort (or OASIS); record's dataset_equal='Yes' unsupported
gates.modality_family: mismatch: diffusion MRI vs EEG (record's P-117); against the pack PDF's MRI-PET the family would partly overlap, but the dataset gate still fails; no waiver on record

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: accuracy (P-117) vs ROC-AUC (P-91); different comparison and population class behind the label 'MCI'
performance_validity: Likely applies to P-117 (claimed 99.81% internal) but unconfirmable without the correct PDF; not needed for the verdict.
grounds: The supplied P-117 PDF is the wrong paper (OASIS MRI-PET fusion), so the 99.81% EEG result cannot be checked from source.
P-91 reports an AUC for Parkinson's-disease MCI vs Parkinson's disease with normal cognition, a different metric, comparison and population from an accuracy for MCI vs healthy controls.
The dataset-family gate fails under either identity of P-117, and the modality gate fails for the EEG paper the record means; no waiver is on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: We found the proposed model as the best classifier with an accuracy of 95.5 %, 94.1 % and 95.9 % in classifying HC vs MCI, MCI vs AD and AD vs HC respectively
Resting-state 19-channel EEG from MCI and healthy participants.
Methods: Forty IPD with normal cognition (IPD-NCI), thirty IPD-MCI, and thirty healthy controls were included.

those DTI measures with statistical difference between PD-MCI and PD- NCI were extracted as features and then with the clinical characteristics were fed into support vector machine (SVM) model to differentiate IPD- NCI from IPD-MCI.
validation dataset: balanced accuracy = 0.79; AUC = 0.80; sensitivity = 0.78; specificity = 0.75

record_defects: P-117's paper_pdf_map entry points to the wrong PDF (MRI-PET S1746809422007662 instead of EEG S1746809423005462).
claim_b 'AUC 0.80 on T1' omits that the comparison is PD-MCI vs PD-NCI within Parkinson's disease.
The earlier rejection reason ('Metric incommensurability: Acc vs AUC') is correct as far as it goes, but it was filed as false_positive; the right category is documented incommensurability.
Registry row P-117: Best_Metric and Dataset 'not reported' despite the 99.81% claim.
resolution_note's bridging list is boilerplate unrelated to either paper.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing plausible: the metric type and the PD-MCI vs PD-NCI comparison make P-91 incommensurable with any MCI-vs-healthy accuracy, whatever the correct P-117 PDF says.
